newsitem.title: UK: U.S. investor claims 1.0 pct of Pearson - FT.
newsitem.headline: U.S. investor claims 1.0 pct of Pearson - FT.

text.p: Michael Price, an activist shareholder in the United States, claims to have taken a 1 percent stake in media and leisure group Pearson Plc, said the Financial Times newspaper.
Price, who had built the stake at a price of less than 700p a share late last year, described the investment as "passive", said the paper.
"We believe that the company has got some of the best assets in financial publishing," the paper quoted him as saying.
Price expected Pearson, itself owner of the Financial Times, to be run better than it had been in the past or face greater pressure to dispose of assets or succumb to an outright sale.
A report that Price's mutual fund group had acquired a shareholding contributed to a 15p gain in the share price to 763-1/2p at the close on Wednesday, said the article.

The investor also told the paper that his investment in Pearson was one of a number he had made in media groups, including Mirror Group and various parts of Conrad Black's empire and reflected a view that "there's value in the industry worldwide".
Despite the small size of the stake Price's emergence will add to pressure on Pearson chief executive Marjorie Scardino, appointed last October, to improve the company's performance, it added.
